result: One family, with a few per-model parameter notes. OpenAI's single GPT-6 prompting section covers Astra, 6.1 Sol, 6.1 Terra and Luna, and every behavior point in it was observed on Astra. Sol, Terra and Luna have no model-specific prompting pages. The Codex GPT-6 prompt text for Luna and Terra was not read.

blockers: none
questions: the brief's model list omits GPT-6 Astra. OpenAI's guidance is written for Astra and extended to the rest, so the writer should decide whether to name Astra.

**Sources (labels used below)**
LM: `https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latest-model.md`. Section "Prompting best practices". Current as of fetch on 2026-11-09. It says "Use the following prompts as a starting point across the GPT-6 model family. They address behavior observed with GPT-6 Astra; evaluate them with your chosen model and workload."
RB: `https://developers.openai.com/blog/rethinking-skills-and-prompts-for-gpt-6-astra` (2026-09-11).
PG: `https://openai.com/index/practical-guide-building-gpt-6/` (2026-10-02).
MJ: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/main/codex-rs/models-manager/models.json`. The `instructions_template` of `gpt-6-astra` and `gpt-6.1-sol` was read; the Luna and Terra entries were not.
MP: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/main/codex-rs/models-manager/prompt.md`. This is the legacy generic Codex prompt, last changed 2026-06-23 per the upd.dev listing. It is not the GPT-6 prompt.
Model pages: `https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6.1-sol`, `.../gpt-6.1-terra`, `.../gpt-6-luna`.
Third party (inference only): `https://harness.dtmont.com/codex/three-model-prompt-comparison/`.

**Family split: one family**
LM states that one prompting section applies "across the GPT-6 model family" and was observed on Astra.
Model IDs are `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6.1-sol`, `gpt-6.1-terra`, `gpt-6-luna` (LM, "Migration quickstart").
The differences that exist are API parameters, not prompt-writing rules (LM, "Limitations" and "Update API and model parameters"):
  - Astra and 6.1 Sol do not support effort `none`; Terra and Luna do.
  - Luna supports Chat Completions function calling only with effort `none`.
  - Sol supports `low` to `max`; Terra and Luna also support `none`.
  - Terra's page advises "Start with `medium` and increase it if the improvement in quality is worth the added time and tokens."
  - Knowledge cutoffs differ: Sol 2026-04-30, Terra 2026-06-01, Luna 2026-05-18 (model pages).
RB, "Better skills": "Guidance that helps Sol or Luna may overconstrain GPT-6 Astra". Smaller models may need more scaffolding than Astra. This is the only OpenAI hint of a per-model prompting difference, and it gives no rules.
Codex ships a separate `instructions_template` per slug (MJ). The third-party hash comparison shows these sizes:

  | Model | Template size |
  |---|---|
  | `gpt-6-luna` | 18,249 bytes |
  | `gpt-6-sol` | 19,207 bytes |
  | `gpt-6-astra` | 21,657 bytes |
  | `gpt-6.1-sol` | 22,011 bytes |

  All other Codex model_messages fields are identical across the four. The Astra and 6.1 Sol text I read opens with the same "You are Codex, an agent based on GPT-6" prompt. What differs in the Luna and Sol 6.0 templates was not read. Inference: the templates are tuned per model but share one structure.
GPT-6 versus GPT-6.1: 6.1 Sol is a drop-in upgrade for `gpt-6-sol`. The only migration note is to review it before switching (LM intro). No prompting difference is stated.
Recommendation (inference): one family, `gpt-6`, with a short "per-model notes" subsection for the effort and API deltas above.

**Guide mapping**

Headings follow the Claude and Kimi guides: Pages, Points (grouped), Gaps.

*A. General principles*
Give a clear assignment: the result, who it is for, context, constraints and what counts as done (PG, "Give the model a clear assignment"). PG quotes Provencher: "overly specific guidance can now hinder results where it previously helped."
Skills and prompts should not be elaborate itineraries or recipes (RB, "Better skills").
Replace "always ask" rules with explicit decision boundaries (PG; RB, "Decision boundaries").
Apply the bias-to-action prompt as the baseline (LM, "Initiative and follow-through").

*B. Output and formatting*
Astra defaults to lists, tables and Markdown. State the prose preference and structure you want (LM, "Personality and writing style"). OpenAI gives paste-in prompts for:
  - clear paragraphs, with lists only for parallel or sequential items;
  - plain language, active voice, main point first;
  - banning stock phrases ("delve", "leverage", "Bottom Line:") and contrastive "X, not Y" framing.
Specify the final report: what changed, what was checked, what still needs attention (PG, "Define the output you need").
Codex's GPT-6 template (MJ, "Writing style" and "Technical communication"):
  - Lead with the outcome.
  - Summarize routine verification instead of listing every check.
  - Write PR descriptions for a reviewer who has not seen the conversation.
  - Use clickable absolute-path file links.
  - Use a CommonMark blank line before lists.

*C. Tool use*
Use the Responses API for tools; Chat Completions tool calling needs it, with the Luna exception above (LM).
Codex GPT-6 rules (MJ, "Rules for getting work done"):
  - Prefer `rg` and `rg --files`.
  - Batch independent reads and searches in parallel and keep dependent steps sequential.
  - Do not chain shell commands with echo separators.
  - Avoid blocking waits over 60 seconds.
  - Treat shell text as code and quote it properly.
Codex sets `apply_patch_tool_type: "freeform"` for `gpt-6-astra` and `gpt-6.1-sol` (MJ). `apply_patch` is a supported Responses tool for Luna (Luna model page). Terra's tool list was not read.
Do not message third parties (Slack, email) without explicit instruction (MJ, "When to ask the user for permission").
Async tool calls and mid-turn steering are API features (LM, "What's new"), so treat them as harness concerns.

*D. Thinking and reasoning*
Effort is set per request, or mid-conversation with `configuration_update` items, which preserve the cache (LM, "What's new").
`xhigh` only when evals justify it (third-party quote of OpenAI's reasoning guide; inference). I did not read the reasoning guide itself.
When effort is not `none`, drop `temperature`, `top_p` and `top_logprobs` (LM). This is an API point, not instruction text.
Codex defaults GPT-6 models to `default_reasoning_level: "low"` and `default_reasoning_summary: "none"` (MJ). Codex also lists `ultra`, "Maximum reasoning with automatic task delegation", which is not in the API docs.

*E. Agentic systems*
Autonomy:
  - Infer intent and persist until the goal is complete.
  - Treat "can you…", "help me…" and "I want to…" as instructions to act.
  - Do not stop at a plan, an offer or a "helpful enough" partial result.
  - Proceed on reversible, read-only, review and fix work (LM; MJ, "Autonomy and persistence").
Approval:
  - Finish the authorized work first so that approval is the final step on a concrete result, for deploys, PR merges, external writes and publishing.
  - Authorization persists across turns.
  - Skip "unsolicited warnings, disclaimers, approval flows, or safety/compliance checklists due to hypothetical risk" (LM; MJ).
Persistence:
  - Define "done" in the prompt: implement, run, inspect and fix failures.
  - A "stop for review after first implementation" rule pulls the model to stop early (RB, "Persistence"; PG).
  - Say where exploration should stop.
Precedence:
  - User instructions outrank skills (LM; MJ).
  - Astra "can be more sensitive" to `AGENTS.md` and skills, and conflicting guidance can make it pause. Audit them.
  - When a skill causes a pause, name the SKILL.md file, quote the line and explain.
Subagents:
  - Astra "may delegate less often than desired", so state when and how much to delegate (LM, "Subagent delegation").
  - OpenAI's prompt: "If at any point you can parallelize work by delegating tasks to another agent… you should do so… if it could save time or improve quality."
  - Inter-agent messages need proper spacing and must stay legible, since a human may read them.
  - Codex's root and subagent roles are in MJ `multi_agent`.
Context and state:
  - Compaction does not end the task; continue from the summary and do not redo work (MJ).
  - The newest user message steers the active task and does not replace it unless it clearly cancels it (MJ).
  - Codex notes a `notes` and `history` workflow for context windows (MJ `token_budget`).
Questions:
  - Bundle questions and prefer multiple choice.
  - Allow about 60 seconds for optional clarifications, then proceed with a stated assumption.
  - Never treat elapsed time as approval for required decisions (MJ, "Working with the user").
Testing and verification:
  - Astra over-tests small tasks.
  - OpenAI's prompt: do not write tests that mirror the implementation for low-impact changes. Run the checks the change needs, then broaden only when new changes, failures or unresolved concerns justify it (LM, "Testing and verification").
  - Previous models needed prodding to test; Astra does not. Remove "always test" lines (RB, "Up-to-date AGENTS.md").

*F. Skill and context-file authoring*
Skill descriptions should be as short as possible while stating when to use the skill. Example: "Use when adding or changing a migration, or reviewing its rollout" (RB).
Use progressive disclosure: a minimal router root with supporting docs loaded on demand.
In `AGENTS.md`, make doc pointers contextual and do not demand "read X, Y, Z before every edit". Authorize safe routine workflows, such as local tests on disposable data (RB; PG).
Lower-confidence point: Codex's GPT-6 prompt sets `include_skills_usage_instructions: false` and carries its own skills section (MJ). I did not read the skills text in full.

*G. Model pages and gaps*
The model pages give per-model facts: context 1,050,000, max output 128,000, effort ranges, and Terra's focus on visual reasoning and computer use.
Gaps:
  - No dedicated Luna or Terra prompting guide was found.
  - The OpenAI reasoning guide was not fetched.
  - The cookbook GPT-5.x Codex prompting guide was not read.
  - The Codex repo has no `core/prompt.md` for GPT-6; the GPT-6 text lives in `models.json`.
  - The Luna and Terra `instructions_template` text, and what changed from 6.0 to 6.1 Sol, were not read.

**Codex prompt conventions (paths)**

GPT-6 text is in `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json`; the legacy prompt is `codex-rs/models-manager/prompt.md`.
AGENTS.md (MP, "AGENTS.md spec"):
  - Scope is the directory tree rooted at the file.
  - Obey every file whose scope covers a touched file.
  - Nested files win.
  - Direct system, developer and user instructions beat AGENTS.md.
  - Root-to-CWD files are preloaded and need no re-reading.
apply_patch:
  - GPT-6 entries are `freeform` (MJ).
  - The legacy prompt gives the patch grammar: Add, Delete and Update File, `@@` hunks, `*** Begin Patch` and `*** End Patch`. It says never use `applypatch` or `apply-patch`, and do not re-read a file after patching (MP).
Planning: `update_plan` has 5 to 7 word steps, exactly one `in_progress`, no filler steps, and no repeating the plan after a call (MP).
Preambles: 1 to 2 sentences before tool calls, grouped and not for trivial reads (MP). The GPT-6 template replaces this with `commentary` and `final` channels. Send a commentary update first when tools are needed, never go over 60 seconds without one, and keep the final answer self-contained (MJ).
Autonomy: see section E above.
Reasoning effort: see section D above.
Review prompts: the guardian classifier lives at `codex-rs/prompts/templates/guardian/classifier_instructions.md`. I did not read a code-review prompt.
Compaction: `codex-rs/prompts/templates/compact/prompt.md` is a handoff summary for another LLM, listing progress, constraints, remaining steps and key data (third-party capture, harness.dtmont.com/codex/codex-cli-prompts).

notes:
Several Codex and OpenAI points correct earlier-model habits, so the writer should not copy them into other families. Examples: "hold off on tests until the user confirms" in MP, and the "bias to action" prompts that exist because Astra over-asks.
HolyAgent's `AGENTS.md` and root rules say to stop and report at a protected boundary. OpenAI's boundary-setting advice matches this: state the boundary explicitly, with the reason, instead of a blanket "always ask".
Ceiling on all behavior points: they come from Astra observations that OpenAI extends to the rest of the family. Evaluate on the target model.
